title: Decoding a Doubled Bit
statement: Let $y$, $pre$, $rest$, and $u$ be binary words, let $b$ be a bit, and suppose $y=pre\,b\,b\,rest$. Starting from the comparator configuration in parser state at input position $|pre|+1$, with decoded work word $u$ and work head at position $|u|$, after two steps it is in parser state at input position $|pre|+3$, with decoded work word $u$ followed by $b$ and work head at position $|u b|$.
replaced: Suppose the comparator input has the form $y = p\,b\,b\,r$ for a bit $b$ and words $p, r$. From the parser state at position $|p|+1$ with decoded word $u$, exactly two steps of the pair comparator append $b$ to the work tape and move to position $|p|+3$, emitting nothing.
